q: A cart is first at the position $x = 5\,\text{m}$ and then at the position $x = -3\,\text{m}$. Calculate the component of the displacement $\Delta x$ with its sign and tell what the sign says about the direction of the displacement vector $\Delta\overline{x}$.
a: $\Delta x = x_2 - x_1 = -3\,\text{m} - 5\,\text{m} = -8\,\text{m}$. As a vector the displacement is $\Delta\overline{x}$, whose $x$-component is $-8\,\text{m}$ and whose length is $|\Delta\overline{x}| = 8\,\text{m}$. The negative sign means that the vector points in the negative direction of the $x$-axis.

q: The $(t, x)$ graphs of three carts are straight lines. One rises more steeply than another, and the third falls. What can be concluded from the graphs about the velocities?
a: The slope is the velocity. A more steeply rising line belongs to a greater velocity in the positive direction. The slope of a falling line is negative, so the third cart moves in the negative direction.

q: You walk $100\,\text{m}$ east along a straight street and return the same distance back to the starting point. What are the distance travelled, the displacement and the average velocity?
a: The distance is $200\,\text{m}$, the displacement is 0 and the average velocity is $v_\text{avg} = \Delta x / \Delta t = 0$. The displacement depends only on the initial and final positions, not on the route.
